steps: Check the site & permit
Ask the authority having jurisdiction about a permit and inspection. Freestanding room heater, not in a sleeping room; fireplace and alcove limits differ between pages (see note).

Freestanding solid-fuel room heater, listed for insulated, habitable rooms. Not for concrete, uninsulated basements or shop/garage spaces: constant over-fire there voids the warranty (p. 16). Label: do not install in a sleeping room; connection through a wall or ceiling requires special methods per local code.

Note: the label on p. 4 says the stove is not to be installed in any fireplace; p. 13 bans alcove and fireplace installs in Canada only and, for the USA, says to adhere to minimum safe clearance dimensions; p. 14 lists the fan kit as required for alcove installations.
Clearances & floor protection

Hold the lettered minimum clearances on the p. 8 drawing. On a combustible floor, fit a non-combustible UL 1618-2009 (Type 1) shield: min. 32" x 40.125" (USA), 16" in front of and 8" beside the loading door.
Combustion air
In tight homes, balance intake air against HRVs, air handlers, range hoods and dryers. A fresh air intake into the stove room is recommended.

Air-tight homes: balance intake air for every exhausting appliance (HRV, constant-run air handler fans, fireplaces, range hoods, dryers). A fresh air intake inlet into the stove room is recommended; without it, air starvation, smoke spillage and carbon monoxide threats may result. Consult an HVAC specialist.

Outside air kit (S.Z1726 / S.Z1726B): flexible metal hose through an exterior wall or up through the floor, structural integrity unchanged, kept open at all times. It must never enter the wall higher than the bottom of the intake air channel on the rear of the stove; it feeds up into that channel.
Connector & venting

6" diameter, 24 MSG steel connector (no aluminum or galvanized), kept direct, every joint fastened with sheet metal screws. Ceiling support package at a ceiling, listed wall thimble through a combustible wall.

Connector required: no chimney directly on the outlet. Double-wall pipe recommended from the stove top adaptor to the ceiling support box. Never run flue pipe through an attic, roof space, closet, concealed space, floor or ceiling. Keep an effective vapor barrier where the chimney exits the structure.

Prefab chimney: support package or wall pass-through and "T", fire stops, insulation shield, flashing and cap all from the same chimney manufacturer. An interior chimney is recommended; build a chase around an exterior one. Never connect to a chimney serving another appliance (voids warranty). Canada: CSA B365-M87.
Masonry chimney (if used)
Have it inspected by a certified professional to NFPA minimums (no cracks, loose mortar, deterioration or blockage) and cleaned first. A stainless steel liner, preferably insulated, is recommended.
Chimney height
Min. 15 ft stove top to termination at 0–1000 ft elevation, more for elbows and altitude. No more than one offset (two elbows).

Recommended minimums by elevation and elbows are in the table on this page (see the Chimney height spec). Above the roof: at least 3ft higher than the highest point where it passes through the roof and 2ft higher than the highest part of the roof or any obstruction within 10ft horizontally (p. 10). Wall exits: a pair of 45° elbows is recommended over a single 90°.

Note: p. 9 recommends a vertical length of 3 ft from stove top to elbow for wall exits; the troubleshooting chart on p. 36 calls for a minimum vertical rise of 36" before elbows.
Fan kit wiring (optional)
Fan kit S.Z2814 has a three-prong grounded plug: straight into a grounded three-hole receptacle, ground prong intact, cord never in front of or under the stove.
Mobile home (if applicable)
Outside air kit required (fitting it first is recommended); double-wall close-clearance flue pipe to a listed UL-103HT chimney, roof exit only. Fasten to the floor with the Z2872 leg anchor kit.

• Outside air kit (S.Z1726 / S.Z1726B) required; installing it before the stove is recommended.
  • Flue pipe double-wall, close-clearance type, CAN/ULC-S629 or ULCS610; single wall not allowed.
  • Listed factory-built chimney for solid fuels, UL-103HT (USA) / CAN/ULC-S629 (Canada); roof exit only; the chimney must be removed to transport the building.
  • Fasten to the floor with the tie-downs in leg anchor kit Z2872. Maintain the structural integrity of floor, wall and ceiling/roof. Only in an open area not used for sleeping.
Note: for mobile homes, the label on p. 4 says outside air kit and fan kit or rear shield required; the clearance table on p. 8 and the text on p. 13 list only the outside air kit; p. 14 says the fan kit is required for mobile home or alcove installations.
Door change-out (if needed)
Remove the thermometer and cast top, the cast sides (two top bolts, 7/16" wrench), then the four bolts on the cast front & door while it is supported (two people). Reverse to install.
Hand-over
Complete the installer notes on the last page (dealer, installer, date installed, serial no.) and leave the manual with the homeowner.

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Use these steps for every cold start. Stay with the stove while the door is open.

  1. Check that all the firebricks are in place. Build the fire on the bottom bricks, with no grate.
  2. Turn the thermostat to High and the fan (if you have one) off.
  3. Open the bypass, then open the loading door.
  4. Put 10 balls of non-glossy paper toward the front. Crisscross 20 pieces of kindling on top, with air gaps.
  5. Light it and leave the door cracked open while it gets going.
  6. When the kindling is fully burning, add two or three medium logs. Keep the door unlatched until they catch.
  7. Latch the door. When the combustor temperature starts to climb, close the bypass. A door left open after the wood catches can wear out the combustor early.
  8. When nearly all the wood is burning and the thermometer reads Active, open the bypass and door and fill the stove, wood as far back as it goes. Latch the door; close the bypass.
  9. Leave it on High until the fire is well established and the needle is in the Active zone (at least 500F).
  10. Then turn the thermostat down gradually to the heat you want.
First fires: curing paint gives off a strong odor and smoke. Burn at a low setting for several hours, with a door or window open until it clears. A paint color change is normal.
Fan kit? The manual gives different times to switch it on; see Thermostat, bypass & fan.

controls.title: Thermostat, bypass & fan
controls.html:
Thermostat

The knob is at the upper right rear corner. At High the stove burns fastest and gives the most heat; turn it counter clockwise for less. Change it gradually: a fast change can make the thermostat work improperly, or let the fire go out. The wood only burns at the rate you set, so a full load won't burn hotter. The lowest setting is fixed at the factory, and it's against federal regulations to alter it.

Bypass

The bypass handle is on the right side. Pointing forward, the bypass is open and smoke temporarily skips the combustor, as when you light or reload. To close it, turn the handle clockwise until it points to the rear, then push down until you hear a click.

Leaving the bypass open too long can cause a run-away fire.

Fan (optional kit)

Keep the fan off until the stove reaches normal operating temperature. About 30 minutes after the fire is established, match the fan speed to the thermostat: low with low, high with high.

Note: the manual gives different times to turn the fan on. The fan section on p. 16 says to keep it off until the stove reaches normal operating temperature; the lighting steps on p. 20 say to turn it on high when you close the bypass (step 7) and to turn it on after the initial warm-up (step 11).

thermometer.title: Reading the catalytic thermometer
thermometer.html:
The dial on top of the stove shows whether the catalytic combustor is working.

Active zoneabove 500F · clean burn
Inactive zonebelow 500F · not a clean burn

Keep the needle in the Active zone. A working combustor stays above 500F and often goes past 1000F. If the needle drops after you turn the thermostat down, turn it back up and let the fire re-establish. For an accurate reading, switch the fan off first.

Note: p. 18 says to turn the fan off for about 5 minutes before reading the thermometer; pp. 29 and 35 say 10 minutes.

Checking the dial itself

Clean the probe regularly, with the fire out and the stove cool. Out of the stove at room temperature for 10 minutes, the needle should point to the bottom of the Inactive zone. If it doesn't, it may need adjustment.

Note: p. 29 gives steps for wiping the probe and re-aligning the dial, then says any thermostat or thermometer maintenance must be completed by a certified installer.

reload.title: Reloading the stove
reload.html:
If the needle is still in the Active zone, reload this way. If it has dropped to Inactive, use the lighting steps instead.

  1. Have the next load ready. Turn the thermostat to High and wait a few minutes for the air flow to settle.
  2. Open the bypass and wait a few more minutes. This cuts down smoke spilling into the room.
  3. With the bypass open, crack the loading door to let room air in. Give it a minute.
  4. Open the door slowly and load. If smoke spills out, close the door slightly until the chimney draws again.
  5. Latch the door and close the bypass right away. Leave it on High until the fire is well established, then turn it down.

On low settings you may see little flame. That's fine: the needle stays Active while the burn continues.

Mild spring and fall days

When it's milder outside, perhaps 55F to 70F, the chimney draws weakly and smoke can spill when you open the door. Run on High for 30 minutes after lighting or reloading, then turn down gradually. If the needle won't stay Active, turn the thermostat up and wait 15 minutes; repeat as needed. Too warm? Burn smaller loads instead of turning the thermostat down.

In extremely cold weather, chimney vapor can freeze and block the chimney. Run on High for 5 to 10 minutes to melt any ice.

wood.title: Choosing firewood
wood.html:
Burn seasoned cordwood only: split, stacked so air reaches all of it, and kept out of rain and snow for at least 24 months. That gets it to 20% moisture or lower. Wet wood wastes heat and builds up creosote.

Never burn wet, green or unseasoned wood. This stove is designed to burn natural wood only. Burning wet wood can cause excessive creosote buildup, and if the creosote ignites, it can cause a chimney fire that may result in a house fire and serious bodily harm. Burning air-dried, seasoned wood lowers the risk of chimney fires and gives higher efficiency and lower emissions.

Hardwood and softwood both burn well. Dense hardwood burns a little slower and longer.

Check it with a moisture meter

  1. Pick three logs at random and split each one down the middle.
  2. On each split face, take three readings: 2" from each end and one in the middle, with the pins in line with the grain.
  3. Average all the readings for a rough answer.

Never burn

Wet, green or unseasoned wood (it builds up creosote and can cause a chimney fire), salt-water driftwood (it corrodes the stove and voids the warranty), treated wood, coal, charcoal, colored paper, cardboard, solvents or garbage (burning these may release toxic fumes and/or carbon monoxide, which may result in poisoning), and flammable fluids such as gasoline, naphtha or engine gel. Never use chemicals or fluids such as gasoline-type lantern fuel, kerosene or charcoal lighter fluid to start or freshen up a fire. Doing so may lead to over-firing, resulting in a house fire and serious bodily harm. Used in excess, offcuts, pressed-wood logs and small, very dry pieces can overheat and damage the firebox.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
The best way to keep the glass clean is to burn on High for a while after each reload. That drives off the moisture that causes most of the film. Leaving the thermostat higher for 30 minutes to an hour before turning it low for an overnight burn also helps.

Long, very low burns leave creosote on the glass. Run on High for about 30 minutes to burn most of it off.

Hand-cleaning heavier deposits

  • Only when the stove and glass are cool. Never clean hot glass.
  • Use a soft cloth. No abrasive cleaners.
  • Rinse well with water afterward. Cleaner left on the glass bakes on and is very hard to remove.
Don't strike the glass or slam the door, and don't use the stove if the glass or its gasket is broken. The warranty covers thermal breakage only, not glass that's struck or cleaned with harsh or abrasive cleaners. Replacement glass must be 5 mm ceramic glass.

ash.title: Removing ashes
ash.html:
Take ashes out whenever they come within one inch of the door opening. Leave a bed about 1/2" thick, because wood burns best on it.

  1. Make sure the fire is out and the stove is cool to the touch.
  2. Put the ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Nothing else goes in it.
  3. Set the closed container on a noncombustible floor or on the ground outside, well away from anything that can burn.
  4. Keep the ashes in the closed container until every cinder is cold, even if you'll bury or spread them.

The fire poker that came with the stove has a hook for pulling the ash plug. The manual's ash-removal section continues on p. 30 without written steps. After the last fire of the season, remove all ash from the firebox and the ash drawer.

Never store hot ashes in a garage or basement. They give off carbon monoxide and flammable gases that can suffocate and kill. Don't vacuum until the stove is cool: hot ash can melt a vacuum and start a fire.

care.title: Combustor, gasket & chimney care
care.html:
Do these through the heating season, always with the stove cool.

  • Combustor: look it over at least three times a season for damage. If ash builds up on its face, lift off the flame shield and brush the face lightly with a soft paint brush, or pass a vacuum wand near it. Never scrape it, push anything into its cells, or take it out to clean it. A hot fire is usually the best cleaner.
  • Door gasket: close the door on a piece of paper (a dollar bill works) and pull it out. No resistance means the door tension needs adjusting. Test all the way around. Don't use the stove if the gasket is missing or damaged.
  • Chimney: slow fires make creosote, which can ignite. Inspect the flue pipe and chimney regularly, especially in the coldest months. Have the chimney and the stove cleaned at least once a year, or as often as needed; a professional chimney sweep is recommended.

At the end of each season, clean out and inspect the stove for warped plates or cracks, and correct any problem before the next season, or the warranty is void.

If the thermometer still won't reach the Active zone after cleaning and reburning, the combustor may need replacing. Blaze King recommends your dealer do that job.

safety.title: Safety & chimney fires
safety.html:
• Keep at least one smoke detector and one carbon monoxide monitor in the room with the stove, and more around the house. If an alarm sounds, get everyone out first, then find the cause.
  • Keep a fire extinguisher in a central spot everyone knows.
  • The stove is hot whenever it's in use. Keep children and pets from touching it.
  • Keep furniture, clothing and other combustibles at least 48" from the front. Don't store wood within the safety clearances or the space you need for loading and ash removal.
  • Run it only with the loading door closed; open it just to add wood.

If a chimney fire or run-away fire starts

  1. Turn the thermostat knob fully counter clockwise. Make sure the loading door and the bypass door are closed.
  2. Call the fire department.
  3. Check the chimney, attic and roof for anything hot enough to catch fire. If needed, use a fire extinguisher or a garden hose.
  4. Don't use the stove again until you're sure the chimney isn't damaged. Have a certified chimney sweep inspect the chimney and flue connector.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Blaze King's limited warranty is for the original purchaser of a stove bought from an authorized dealer and installed in the USA or Canada. It starts on the date of purchase and can't be transferred.

All parts and materials, incl. exterior paint1 year
Fan assemblies, modular thermostat, door handle steel parts2 years
Stove body, accessories, steel firebox parts5 years
Catalytic combustor6 years

The longer terms are pro-rated. On the 5-year coverage you pay 20% of the then-current retail cost in year 2, 40% in year 3, 60% in year 4 and 80% in year 5. The combustor is free for three years, then you pay 60%, 70% and 80% in years 4 to 6; a claim needs the combustor, a combustor failure report and proof of purchase.

Not covered

  • Gaskets and firebrick, and normal wear such as paint discoloration
  • Over-firing (warped plates, burnt-off paint) and wrong fuels such as driftwood or treated wood
  • Chimney-fire damage, transit damage, and installs not to local codes

Report a problem to your dealer within 30 days of finding it, with proof of purchase. Mail in the warranty registration card.

specHeight.title: Recommended chimney height
specHeight.html:
Minimum recommended vertical height, stove top to termination, by elevation and elbows (0 / 2 x 15° / 2 x 30° / 2 x 45°):

0–1000 ft15 / 16 / 18 / 19 ft
1000–2000 ft15.5 / 16.5 / 18.5 / 19.5 ft
2000–3000 ft16 / 17 / 19 / 20 ft

The table continues to 8000 ft. Add 2.0 ft per 90° elbow and 3.0 ft per "T"; 1.0 ft of horizontal run = 2 ft of vertical rise (sea-level example: 15.0 + 2.0 + 4.0 + 3.0 = 24.0 ft). No more than one offset (two elbows); two 45° elbows equal one 90°. These figures are only guidelines; see draft performance (p. 9). Above the roof: 3ft over the roof penetration and 2ft over anything within 10ft (p. 10).

Note: p. 9 recommends a vertical length of 3 ft from stove top to elbow for wall exits; the troubleshooting chart on p. 36 calls for a minimum vertical rise of 36" before elbows.

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
Minimum clearances are printed as lettered dimensions (A, B, C, D, E, F, J, with footnoted G, H, I, K, L) keyed to the drawing on this page and on the label (p. 4). The text does not say what each letter measures, so take the values from the drawing. One set of values covers roof or wall exit, parallel or corner; mobile home installs use the same values, roof exit only.

Single-wall pipe (Canada)18" (450 mm) minimum
Combustible objects, front48" (1219 mm), p. 21

Clearances may only be reduced by means approved by the regulatory authority. Pipe clearances: local codes and the pipe manufacturer's specs.

specFloor.title: Floor protection
specFloor.html:
No thermal hearth pad is required, but on a combustible floor a non-combustible floor shield must be used. It needs no insulation value but must be listed under UL 1618-2009 (Type 1).

Minimum size (USA)32" x 40.125" (813 mm x 1019 mm)
Minimum size (Canada)42.75" x 50.125" (1086 mm x 1273 mm)
USA, from the loading door16" out front · 8" either side
Canada (CSA B365)18" (450 mm) on door sides · 8" (200 mm) other sides
Under the chimney connectorat least 2" either side

Canada: the 18" ember protection spans the full width of the stove plus the 8" each side; within 8" of a wall the pad need only reach the wall. No ember pad on carpet unless structurally supported. Blaze King does not recommend adhesive-based vinyl flooring in front of the stove.

conflicts.issue: Listing standards: certification label gives UL 1482-11(R2022) & CAN/ULC-S627:2023; preface says tested and listed to CAN/ULC-S628:2022 & UL1482-11 (R2022).
Combustor part number: label gives combustor OEM part number Z0336A-M; combustor warranty section and parts list give S.CAT203032.
conflicts.reason: Two numbering systems: the certification label (p. 4) prints the combustor OEM part number Z0336A-M; p. 26 and the parts list (p. 37) give Blaze King's own part number for the combustor assembly, S.CAT203032. Both are shown in specParts, each labelled.

conflicts.issue: Fan-off time before reading the catalytic thermometer: approximately 5 minutes (p. 18) vs 10 minutes (calibration note p. 29, troubleshooting p. 35).
Catalytic thermometer maintenance: p. 29 gives owner steps to clean the probe and re-align the dial, then says any thermostat or thermometer maintenance must be completed by a certified installer.

Fan timing at start-up: p. 16 says fans off until normal operating temperature, then about 30 minutes after the fire is established match fan speed to the thermostat; lighting step 7 (p. 20) says turn fans on high when the bypass is closed; step 11 says turn the fan on after the initial warm-up.

Mobile-home kit requirements: label says outside air kit and fan kit or rear shield required; p. 8 table and p. 13 list only the outside air kit; p. 14 says the fan kit is required for mobile home or alcove installations. No rear shield part is listed anywhere.

Fireplace/alcove installs: label says not to be installed in any fireplace; p. 13 prohibits alcove and fireplace installs in Canada only and tells USA installers to adhere to minimum clearances; p. 14 mentions alcove installations (fan kit required).

Vertical rise before the first elbow: p. 9 recommends 3 ft from stove top to elbow (wall exit); p. 36 troubleshooting says a minimum vertical rise of 36" before elbows. The clearance drawings (pp. 4, 8) also carry labels reading 'MIN.2ft*' and '*3ft recommended'.

review.notes: Clearances to combustibles (A, B, C, D, E, F, J and footnoted G, H, I, K, L) exist only as a lettered table keyed to the clearance drawing (pp. 4, 8); the text never defines the letters, so no lettered values were transcribed.
